correctness.rationale: For an unselected cell the number of fort neighbors is the sum of its incidence degrees. Exactly the zero/one pair is forbidden, making the two side-coverage conditions necessary and sufficient. If both sides are covered, minimality requires a minimal edge cover, hence stars. A leaf in each class prevents a one-side-covering proper subfort, and a subfort omitting vertices on both sides would require a cycle. If there are no leaves on one side, its stars must all have two edges: degree ≥3 allows a deletion, and degree exactly two forces any proper subset either to leave a degree-one covered vertex opposite an isolate, or to omit an entire row or column opposite degree-one vertices. If just one side is covered, its vertices must all have degree two by deletion; a contained cycle is a fort, otherwise every proper subset that could be a fort would omit vertices on both sides and require a cycle. If both sides have isolates a cycle is necessary. A proper subset of a nonspanning simple cycle can neither keep an entire required side covered in degree two nor contain a cycle; a cycle spanning both sides contains a perfect matching and is not minimal. Counting star components by labeled sets gives S−B−C and the two degree-two exceptions, counted by pairing labeled leaves at each prescribed center. Suppression of the covered side in a subdivision forest gives distinct labeled edges of a simple forest, with an isolate still present. Cayley and subtraction of the no-isolate EGF give U. Alternating undirected cycles on fixed labels have k!(k−1)!/2 orders. For p≤q there are spanning forests of size q (one row star and p−1 single edges) and of size p+q−2 (complementary row- and column-centered stars); subdivision forests have 2p edges and require q≥p+2; cycles top out at 2p off the square diagonal and 2p−2 on it when present. This checks both extrema, including 2×2 and 2×3. My independent subset-DAG check matched the polynomial on all ten frozen boards and two transposes (1,189,956 subsets), and the set classification both ways on boards with at most 16 cells. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/reproduce_frozen.py rook; log /workspace/branches/reproduction-rook.txt. These checks are finite, not a replacement for the coverage and counting arguments.

evidence: The star generating function is the same, with the mirror adding back exp(xy²z²/2) and exp(yx²z²/2). Extraction on p,q≥2 gives precisely q!/2^p if q=2p or p!/2^q if p=2q, at the appropriate z-degrees.

In the mirror's subdivision term (e^y−1)(e^(T(y,x,z))−1), an isolated column contributes y and a nontrivial column tree with k vertices contributes k^(k−2)y^k(xz²)^(k−1)/k!. This is exactly the isolated-vertex forest EGF U after substituting t=xz²; the removed edgeless term has x-degree zero. Extraction multiplies by p!q!, giving p!U(q,p)z^(2p). The transpose agrees.
The mirror's cycle term (e^(x+y)−1)Σ_(k≥2)(xyz²)^k/(2k) gives the binomial choice times k!(k−1)!/2 coefficient and omits exactly the cycles using all labels on both sides.

evidence: With (m,n)=(p,q), the mirror's three families are the frozen four with row and column subdivisions combined. In spanning star covers, no degree-one row means all centers are rows and none are single edges; the mirror excludes exactly those covers having a star of degree ≥3 in this case. The other orientation is symmetric.

The transposed contracted forest conditions match precisely: parallel contracted edges give a four-cycle in the incidence graph. The mirror excludes cycles covering both sides completely, just as the frozen record does.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The line-graph and row-column descriptions have identical vertex and label sets. Grouping the two transposed subdivision cases does not change the classification or scope.
